text: Working with APIs is an essential skill for modern developers. An API allows two programs to communicate with each other. To get data, your application sends HTTP requests to a server, usually using methods like GET or POST. The server often responds with JSON, a simple format that is easy to read and parse. Before you can access protected data, you usually need authentication, such as an API key or a token. It is also important to respect rate limits, which control how many requests you can make in a certain time. Finally, always add error handling to your code, because requests can fail for many reasons.
